title: A night shift on Blackwater Lake
text: Cowork handed over a brief for a co-op horror fishing game. Fable 5.2 studied the biggest Roblox and Steam horror games and kept what makes them work: monsters with rules you learn by dying (DOORS, Pressure), a quota job and greed (Lethal Company), light as safety (99 Nights in the Forest), and a rulebook to check. The twist: the frog chorus is your only danger meter, the owner rewrites his rules between runs, and a fish that is not in the book pays triple. Title: Don't Wave Back.

stills.caption: Concept art for the Lantern Noir look, drawn by Gemini's image model for Liam's style board. The target, not the game.

title: An empty place that builds itself
text: Its own repo, a Rojo project, pinned tools, a one-command gate (lint, format, tests, lints, build, a smoke test of the built place) and CI. The first Studio test: launch our own window, attach, play, call a debug scenario, read a clean console, stop. It worked on the first try, and showed nothing but an avatar in a daytime sky.

stills.caption: The very first play. Nothing built yet.

title: Sound first
text: Ninety-seven sounds written as prompts and generated with ElevenLabs, three takes each, ranked by Gemini with the takes shuffled so it cannot favor the first one. The thinned-out frog loops came back too busy, so the chorus is now built from single frog calls placed along the shore, which thin out exactly as danger rises. An older man's voice was designed for the owner's cassette tapes. 68 sounds and tapes are uploaded to Roblox and proven to play.

title: From pure black to a foggy night
text: The whole lake is built from code: water, shore, dock, bait shack, beacon, sunken steeple, buoy, reeds. The first night was pure black. Three lighting passes in Studio, steered by Gemini Neon's look review (2.5 out of 10 at first, phone readability 2), lifted the fog, warmed the lantern, found a bug where the lantern's own glow blocked its light, and turned the trees into crooked silhouettes.

stills.caption: First night. You can see the HUD and nothing else.
Ambient light raised: the boat appears.
The dock, shack and beacon from the water.
Far out at the sunken steeple.
Too far: the fog turned daytime teal.

Crooked trees, conifers and dead snags against the fog band.

title: A quiet night, start to finish
text: Cast, wait for the bobber tap, reel inside a wandering band, hold the catch up to the lantern and check it against the Field Guide. A Studio bot played a whole six-minute Night 1 through the real controls: six fish, seven of seven points banked at the dock, nothing lost, cleared at 5 AM. A fish that is not in the book is easy to spot: this one glows.

stills.caption: A wrong Pumpkinseed. The Field Guide says nothing in the book glows.

title: Five Lake Rules, tested before they are seen
text: The scare director and all five rules are built as pure logic and tested in simulation first: 145 tests, 2,500 simulated nights with no scare ever inside a guaranteed quiet stretch. A crew that follows the rules survives every night; a crew that ignores them loses someone almost every night. After a design review by Gemini Neon, the Neighbor now hunts lantern light and fakes a crewmate's callout, and nights are six minutes. Putting the rules on screen is next.

title: The rules show up, and Neon watches them
text: The five Lake Rules now play in Studio: the Hum rises under the hull, the Neighbor rows out of the fog with its own lantern, something knocks from below, a tall figure waits in the trees. A bot plays each rule right and wrong, and the clips go to Gemini Neon, which can watch video with sound. Its first verdict on the Hum fail was 3.5 out of 10: you could not see anything happen, the motor that killed you made no sound, and the owner's tape talked over the warning. The fixes are in progress: a visible capsize and underwater plunge, moonlight so the boat reads with the lantern out, motor sound and a motor light on the HUD, and death cards that say what to do next time. The drowned players' bell was also redone by filtering it to sound like it rings underwater.

stills.caption: The Neighbor: another lantern in the fog, and someone in the boat, waving.

title: Five nights, a title screen and a way home
text: The whole game now has its shape. A title screen with a difficulty choice, a Locker for earned cosmetics and a board for the longest Endless night. The rulebook taped inside the boat, with the owner's corrections in red ink that change from run to run. Five nights in a row with retries, and the finale: at 4 AM the dock bell rings by itself and you run for home with the owner's fish. A test bot played a whole five-night run in Studio without losing anyone, and the finale cleared at dawn. Saves fall back to memory until the game is published. Along the way a Gemini Hydrogen review found a real loophole (waiting out a scare in the dock light), now closed: scares pause in the light and fish do not bite near the dock. Behind the scenes, Roblox's monthly upload limit ran out, so 28 missing sounds are rebuilt inside the game from ones already uploaded, and a listening test by Neon led to a new mix where the scare cues cut through the frogs.

stills.caption: The title screen, first version. The panels will shrink so the lake shows.
The rulebook on night 5. The owner has amended Rule 3 in red ink.

title: The bell, the run home, and dawn
text: The finale went through six versions tonight, each one recorded in Studio and watched by Neon. The biggest fix was not in the finale at all: the first-person view did not turn with the boat, so after turning for home you stared at the side of the boat. Now the view turns with the boat, and at the first toll of the bell it swings round to face the dock. The bell rings three times after real silence, the lantern throws light ahead, strange boats and false beacons cross the way home, and reaching the dock with the owner's fish brings the dawn. Neon's finale score went from 1.5 to 3 out of 10, and the Hum's fail from 3.5 to 5; the critic is harsh and sometimes contradicts itself, so its notes are weighed, not obeyed. The phone layout was checked on the smallest phone Roblox offers and rebuilt so every button sits on the right and the steering stick stays clear.

stills.caption: 4 AM: the bell.
The run home, lit by the lantern, the dock light ahead.
Dawn. You made it home.
The smallest phone: buttons on the right, steering stick clear.
A shadow from the lantern post used to black out the middle of the boat.

title: Three polish rounds, an outside audit, and the night is done
text: The last stretch was all finish. Three rounds of polish from Neon's video reviews: the capsize now throws real gear away from the camera and holds the boat on its side until the screen goes dark; the death card is big enough to read on a phone; the lantern really goes dark when it is out, while the moon keeps the boat readable; the dawn eases in instead of popping; the bell, the red oil bar and the turn toward home land as one beat; and small Motor and Lantern buttons now sit beside the book. Then a reviewer that had never seen the build audited the whole game against the brief's safety checks. It found one real fairness hole: on your own, the Watcher could take a player who never saw it if the one who did had already drowned. That is fixed and now checked on every simulated night: every player a rule takes heard its warning first. Neon's scores ended at 5 out of 10 for both big moments, up from 1.5 and 3.5. The strange boats on the run home are still the weakest part, and they are first on the list for next time.

stills.caption: The Hum: lantern out, the moon keeps the boat readable.
A death card big enough for a phone, naming the rule you broke.
4 AM: silence, then the bell, and the turn toward home.
Nearly home: the dock lights and the first grey of dawn.
Dawn, eased in over three seconds.
The run cleared, with the owner's dry thanks.

title: The strange boats, readable at last
text: On the run home the strange boats used to be a dot and a smudge, easy to mistake for a false beacon. Now each one is a boat you can read from across the lake: the hull lies side-on, a man too tall for it stands in a long coat and a wide hat with no face to see, and his lantern hangs by his shoulder in a small amber glow. Boats ahead also come in farther down the way home, so they sit in front of you for a few seconds before you pass. Where the lake places them, and how close is too close, did not change. The Gemini critic went from 2 to 7 out of 10 on 'is it a boat' over four rounds.
